messages:
maria: Heads-up — sketching a calibration dataset + prompt curation plan for the upcoming quant bakeoff (FP8 / INT8 / GPTQ / AWQ). Looking for quick feedback before I lock sizes and strata. TL;DR below, details after.

kevin: +1 to doing stratified by intent. Can you drop expected token-length bands? also we need to pin random seed in every run. :+1:

maria: Plan: 3-part calib bank — A) Core domain (in-distribution app prompts) B) Long-tail misc + low-frequency intents C) Adversarial/paraphrase stress set. Size targets: A=5k, B=2k, C=1k. Holdouts: 10% within each stratum for sanity checks. Token-length bands: short (<32), mid (32-128), long (128-512). We'll sample proportionally across bands. Seed: `42` across all tooling.

sasha: Quick Q — for B (long-tail) do we include user typos and code snippets? that usually breaks quantized models more.

kevin: definitely include typos and mixed-language. For code snippets, mark them as a separate tag so we can analyze by feature.

maria: yes to both. B will have sub-tags: `typo`, `code`, `cli`, `non-english`. We'll store tags as CSV metadata.

maria: Proposed prompt curation heuristics:
- Prefer real user traffic where available (scrubbed) over synthetic.
- For synthetic augmentation use 1 paraphrase + 2 adversarial edits per anchor.
- Ensure each anchor has at least one minimal prompt to check for prefix caching regressions.
- For model-agnostic evals include both single-turn and multi-turn variants (up to 5 turns).

tom: For calibration sets we should also include a small "anchor suite" of 200 golden examples (human-verified) that we always run. These are the canonical regression checks. Put them in `anchors/200-gold.csv`.

anya: Concern: if we sample core domain from recent prod logs we might amplify any label bias. Suggest we stratify core by month and by product subdomain to surface distro shifts. Also add a noise baseline (synthetic nonsense) to detect hallucination spikes.

maria: Good call. Update: core stratified by month (last 6 months) and product. We'll add 500 synthetic-nonsense negative controls.

kevin: How are we going to compute accuracy deltas across quant types? propose: token-level perplexity + task-specific metrics (e.g., F1 for extraction tasks, top-1 accuracy for classification). Report both mean delta and 95th percentile regression.

maria: Agreed. Also include automatic BLEU/EM where appropriate and per-length breakdowns. We'll compute delta vs FP16 baseline.

eval-bot: CI run scheduled: https://ci.redwood.internal/quant-bakeoff/1981234567 — logs will appear in ~45m. Config: `--seed 42 --holdout 0.1 --anchors anchors/200-gold.csv --bands short,mid,long`

maria: Next steps: i'll finalize sampling scripts and upload CSV manifests to the shared drive by EOD. Volunteers for sanity labeling on C (adversarial) set? need ~6 ppl for 2h. @kevin @sasha you two in?

kevin: I can take one session tomorrow 9-11am PT.

sasha: I'll join the other slot.

tom: Added `anchors/200-gold.csv` skeleton to the repo, pls fill columns: id, prompt, tags, expected_output, notes. PR: https://git.redwood/eng-ml/anchor-suite/pull/12

maria: Awesome. I’ll post a final checklist after the CI completes and we have the first quant metrics. Thanks all :rocket:
